community_method: Louvain (networkx) on the weighted kNN graph, seed 42; community 0 is the largest. Negative similarities are clipped to 0 for community detection only.
layout_format: little-endian float32 pairs (x, y) in node order; node i occupies bytes 8*i to 8*i+7. The phone graph uses the first phone-cap entries.
layout_method: ForceAtlas2 (networkx, scaling ratio 10, strong gravity 0.05, node mass 1 + weighted degree) run separately inside each Louvain community for the stated iterations, starting from seeded random points; each community is scaled by the square root of its size and the communities are placed on a sunflower spiral (largest at the centre); the whole layout is scaled to [-1, 1]. Edges between communities do not shape the layout.
quality_rule: embedding_quality is ok when the language is en and low otherwise. The model is English-only, so non-English works are kept and marked low rather than dropped.
selection_rule: A work is a candidate when a pollution-core v0 term matches its title or abstract (whole word, case-insensitive) and its title or abstract is non-empty. The latest raw page holding a work decides it. Candidates are sorted by cited-by count (most first, ties by OpenAlex id); the first 15,000 are embedded and kept.
similarity_rule: Text is the title and abstract. Embeddings come from BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (an English model), L2-normalised; similarity is the cosine. Each node keeps its 5 most similar other nodes (ties: lower node index); edges are the union of those pairs, weight rounded to 3 decimals. The phone file recomputes the 3 most similar nodes inside its 5,000 nodes alone. Over the BQ-V.0 edge budget (desktop 60,000, phone 15,000), the weakest edges (ties: higher node indices first) are dropped while both ends keep another edge.
title_rule: title is the stored title, truncated to 160 characters (159 plus an ellipsis when longer).
what_this_is: Similarity graph of unscreened global OpenAlex query hits on the pollution-core backbone (plastic query version in this manifest). A node is a work; an edge joins two works whose title-and-abstract embeddings are among each other's most similar works, and its weight is their cosine similarity. It is not a citation network, not a screened corpus and not a measure of quality. It holds no abstracts, author names, author IDs, ORCIDs or institution strings. The desktop file holds the 15,000 most cited backbone works; the phone file is the first 5,000 of them.
